rows.grounds: sandhi fusion mohayet + cañcalāpāṅgi; mohayet optative of muh 'to delude/enchant'; cañcalāpāṅgi vocative addressing the beloved
object of mohayet; name of the fierce deity
compound describing rudraṃ: kāla-anala-prabha 'having radiance like the fire of time/dissolution'

items.question: Can the practitioner of the fifty-letter rite enchant even Rudra who shines like the fire of dissolution?
premises: The preceding verses state that a person performs the fifty-letter arrangement in the supreme six-chakra locus.
Such a practitioner gains the power to enchant or delude.
Rudra, radiant like the fire of time, is named as the object of this enchanting power.
items.inference: Therefore, the efficacy of the fifty-letter practice is so great that it can overpower even Rudra in his fearsome, dissolution-fire aspect.
uncertainties: Whether mohayet implies literal bewitchment, ritual subjugation, or a figurative expression of mastery is not specified in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: O you of tremulous eyes, such a person could enchant even Rudra, who shines with the splendor of the fire of time.
